propositions: Blocking-link comparability was decided from a ticket's type tier instead of its position in the parent hierarchy, so requested edges could be silently rewritten.
A ticket could end up with a blocking edge to its own ancestor or descendant, distorting ready, next-batch, and the parent-first claim cascade.
Comparability should be structural (nearest common ancestor) so any two tickets sharing a parent may hold a dependency, replacing the type-tier rule.
An invariant makes ancestor-blocking edges unrepresentable regardless of the path into the resolver, while retaining cross-subtree auto-escalation and its redirect record.
Blocking edges already written under the old type-tier rule must be detectable store-wide and repairable in a single pass via rebar doctor.
Escalation redirect records are discarded on the library and MCP paths because link_core runs quiet, causing silent link substitution for agent callers.
